title: QuadraticFiniteSum.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of an L-smooth quadratic objective on a complete real Hilbert space. Individual quadratic components may be nonconvex, but their average is convex.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: The average operator satisfies ⟨x,(n⁻¹∑ᵢAᵢ)x⟩ ≥ μ‖x‖² for every x, so the objective is μ-strongly convex. Parameters satisfy 0<μ≤L.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: f(x)=n⁻¹∑ᵢ[⟨x,Aᵢx⟩/2+⟨bᵢ,x⟩], with n≥1. Each Aᵢ is a bounded symmetric linear operator with ‖Aᵢ‖≤L.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query chooses any component i and point x and returns exactly Aᵢx+bᵢ. Replies have no error, noise, or dependence on call index or seed. All Params, including n,L,μ,R,G,ε,x0 and the ambient space, are public; Aᵢ and bᵢ are hidden. Oracle budgets count individual component queries and are fixed for every seed.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/QuadraticFiniteSum.lean: spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Quadratic components may have indefinite Hessians; only their average must be positive definite. A minimizer x⋆ exists with ∑ᵢ(Aᵢx⋆+bᵢ)=0, ‖x0−x⋆‖≤R, and maxᵢ‖Aᵢx⋆+bᵢ‖≤G, where R,G≥0 are public. The gradient bound holds at the minimizer, not globally. No finite-dimensionality or separability assumption is imposed.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a measurable Hilbert-space-valued output X whose objective gap relative to a global minimizer is integrable and satisfies E[f(X)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, with ε>0. No particular iterate or averaging rule is required.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee is an expectation under the product of the algorithm and oracle seed laws. Algorithmic randomization is permitted despite exact oracle replies.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/QuadraticFiniteSum.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm.law, Oracle.law, Convergence.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Strongly convex quadratic finite-sum minimization with exact component gradients, an initial-distance bound, and expected objective-gap accuracy is an established optimization formulation, including variants permitting nonconvex components.

descriptionHtml:
Quadratic Finite-Sum Minimization

We consider minimizing f=n−1∑i=1nfi on a real Hilbert space E, where n≥1 and each fi:E→R is quadratic. Component Hessians have operator norm at most L>0, and their average is bounded below by μI, where 0<μ≤L and I is the identity on E. A given point x0∈E satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R for the minimizer x⋆, with R≥0 and ∥∇fi(x⋆)∥≤G for G≥0. The oracle returns ∇fi(x) at a queried pair (i,x). For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with integrable objective gap satisfying EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

Write the component objectives and their average as fi(x)=12⟨x,Aix⟩+⟨bi,x⟩,i=1,…,n,f(x)=1n∑i=1nfi(x), where each Ai:E→E is a bounded linear operator and bi∈E. The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. The algorithm receives E, n, L, μ, R, G, ε, and x0; the operators Ai and vectors bi are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Component curvature and strong convexity). For every i∈{1,…,n}, the operator Ai is symmetric and bounded by L: ⟨Aix,y⟩=⟨x,Aiy⟩,x,y∈E,∥Ai∥op≤L. The average curvature satisfies 1n∑i=1n⟨x,Aix⟩≥μ∥x∥2,x∈E.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance and component gradients). There exists x⋆∈E such that ∑i=1n(Aix⋆+bi)=0,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,∥Aix⋆+bi∥≤G,i=1,…,n. The curvature condition makes x⋆ the unique global minimizer of f.

At any selected index i∈{1,…,n} and point x∈E, the oracle returns the exact component gradient ∇fi(x)=Aix+bi. After the allotted component-gradient calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its objective gap must be integrable under P, and it must satisfy EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

  • James W. Daniel. The Conjugate Gradient Method for Linear and Nonlinear Operator Equations. 1967. Complexity: O(n[1+L/μlog⁡(LR2/ε)]) exact component-gradient calls using conjugate gradients for objective gap at most ε, including initialization and component queries implementing operator products; 0<ε<LR2/2.

comparisonHtml:
On a real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, let F(x)=n−1∑i=1n(⟨x,Aix⟩/2+⟨bi,x⟩), where n≥1, Ai=Ai∗, ∥Ai∥≤L, and n−1∑iAi⪰μI, with 0<μ≤L. Components may be indefinite. A minimizer x∗ satisfies ∥x0−x∗∥≤R and maxi∥Aix∗+bi∥≤G, with R,G≥0. The exact oracle returns Aix+bi; n,L,μ,R,G,ε are supplied. Target: E[F(xout)−F(x∗)]≤ε. Row (1) constructs constant-step random reshuffling with independent uniform permutations per epoch; the setup imposes no algorithm restriction. Comparisons below use 0<ε<LR2.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Symmetric
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Basic

open MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.QuadraticFiniteSum

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  n : ℕ
  [nonzero : NeZero n]
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  G : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE
  Params.measurableE Params.borelE Params.nonzero

structure Instance (q : Params) where
  A : Fin q.n → q.E →L[ℝ] q.E
  b : Fin q.n → q.E

noncomputable def objective {q : Params} (f : Instance q) (x : q.E) : ℝ :=
  (q.n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, (⟪x, f.A i x⟫ / 2 + ⟪f.b i, x⟫)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance := Instance
  Query q := Fin q.n × q.E
  Reply q := q.E
  Output q := q.E
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 < q.μ ∧ q.μ ≤ q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.G ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f oracle :=
    (∀ i, (f.A i).toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) ∧
    (∀ i, ‖f.A i‖ ≤ q.L) ∧
    (∀ x, q.μ * ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ (q.n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, ⟪x, f.A i x⟫) ∧
    (∀ k seed i x, oracle.answer k (0, (i, x)) seed = f.A i x + f.b i) ∧
    (∃ xstar, (∑ i, (f.A i xstar + f.b i)) = 0 ∧
      ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R ∧ ∀ i, ‖f.A i xstar + f.b i‖ ≤ q.G)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn (objective f) Set.univ xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => objective f (output ω) - objective f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, objective f (output ω) - objective f xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.QuadraticFiniteSum
